steps: Run Adobe's Migration Assessment on your Commerce on Cloud or on-premises project and review its complexity rating with your team.
List the custom code, extensions, data in custom tables and integrations that move, and what each becomes on Commerce as a Cloud Service.
Agree the phases, the order of work and who does what between Adobe, your engineering team and us, and write the move plan.
deliverables: Inventory of code, extensions, data and integrations to move
asks: Access to your Commerce project for the assessment
Your engineering lead and platform owner for the planning sessions
risk: A plan that misses custom work: we list every extension, custom table and integration from the assessment before the phases are agreed.
outcome: You know what moves to Commerce as a Cloud Service, in what order, who does each part and how big the move is.

steps: Sort your customizations and extensions into those Commerce as a Cloud Service already covers and those to rebuild.
Rebuild each remaining customization as an App Builder app on Commerce APIs, events and webhooks, starting from the Commerce Developer Agent where it helps.
Review all generated code before it goes near production, and test each app against the agreed behavior.
Deploy the apps to each environment and hand over how each one is built and run.
deliverables: App Builder apps for each rebuilt customization
asks: The current behavior of each customization, with an owner who can confirm it
Access to your App Builder organization and Commerce environments
risk: Behavior lost in the rebuild: we test each app against the behavior your owners agreed before the old code is retired.
outcome: Your customizations run as App Builder apps that keep working as Adobe upgrades Commerce as a Cloud Service.

steps: Set up your store settings and system configuration on the new instance before any data moves.
Move products, customers and orders with Adobe's bulk data migration tool, which Adobe provides through its Commerce Deployed Engineering engagement.
Build an App Builder job for data that third-party extensions hold in custom tables.
Reconcile record counts and spot-check records with your team, then repeat the run for cutover.
deliverables: Store settings set on the new instance
asks: Read access to your current Commerce database
Your data owners to check the spot samples
risk: Missing or mismatched records after the move: we reconcile counts and spot-check records before each run is signed off.
outcome: Your products, customers and orders are on Commerce as a Cloud Service, checked against the old platform.

steps: List every back-office integration and storefront connection that changes with the move.
Re-establish each integration on the new instance through Commerce APIs, events and App Builder.
Point the storefront at the new instance and test every data flow end to end with your system owners.
deliverables: Integrations rebuilt on the new instance
asks: Owners and test accounts for each connected system
risk: An integration that breaks at cutover: we test every data flow end to end before the switch.
outcome: Your back-office systems and storefront work with Commerce as a Cloud Service the way they worked before.

steps: Plan and rehearse the cutover with your team, with a go and no-go list.
Run the final data sync, switch traffic to Commerce as a Cloud Service and check orders, payments and search on the live store.
Retire the old platform and hand over to ongoing operation.
asks: A cutover window agreed with your business
People on call from each connected system on cutover day
risk: Orders lost during the switch: we rehearse the cutover and check live orders and payments straight after it.
outcome: Your store runs on Commerce as a Cloud Service and the old platform is retired.

steps: Agree each brand, store or region to add, with its domain, languages, currencies, tax rules, stock and payment and shipping options.
Add each website, store and store view on the same Admin, with a store view for each language and the allowed currencies and rates.
Set the tax rules, inventory sources and stock, and the local payment and shipping options for each one.
Place a test order in each store and fix what the tests find.
deliverables: Websites, stores and store views set up
Currencies, tax, stock and local options for each
asks: Your list of brands, regions and languages, with their rules
Your tax and finance owner for each region
risk: A region that charges the wrong tax or currency: we place a test order in each store before launch.
outcome: Each brand, store and region runs from one Commerce Admin with its own languages, currencies, tax and stock.

steps: Agree the search facets, synonyms and merchandising rules with your merchandisers.
Set the catalog views, policies, facets, synonyms and rules on Commerce as a Cloud Service.
Test search, category browse and filters on the storefront with your team.
asks: Your merchandisers for the search and rules sessions
risk: Search results shoppers do not expect: we test the agreed searches on the storefront with your merchandisers.
outcome: Search, filters and merchandising on your Commerce as a Cloud Service storefront follow the rules your merchandisers agreed.

steps: Turn on company accounts, shared catalogs, quotes and purchase orders on Commerce as a Cloud Service.
Create the first company accounts with credit limits and custom pricing.
Test company roles, quotes and approvals with your sales team.
asks: Your first buyer companies, with their pricing and credit limits
risk: Buyers who see the wrong prices: we test each first company account against its agreed pricing.
outcome: Your business buyers order from company accounts with their own catalogs, prices, quotes and approvals.

steps: Each month, check capacity and scale the servers for the traffic ahead.
Run backups and a disaster recovery test, and watch the monitoring and alerts.
Apply security patches for the operating system, PHP, database and middleware, and report what changed.
asks: Access to your servers and hosting provider
risk: A slow or unsafe store from servers nobody watches: we check capacity, backups and patches every month.
outcome: Your on-premises Commerce servers stay fast, backed up and patched.

steps: Set up your sandbox and production Commerce Optimizer instances and match each to the commerce and storefront environments of the same kind.
Add your users in the Adobe Admin Console with the roles each team needs.
Record the instance IDs and endpoints for the build team.
asks: Your Adobe Admin Console administrator
risk: Test data showing on the live store: we connect sandbox instances only to test environments and production to production.
outcome: Your teams sign in to Commerce Optimizer with the right roles, on instances matched to each environment.

steps: Agree the catalog views your brands, markets, languages or sales channels need, with your merchandisers.
Set the policies that filter what each view shows and the price books each view uses.
Check each view returns the agreed products and prices.
deliverables: Policies and price books set up
asks: Your merchandisers and pricing owner
risk: A channel that shows the wrong assortment or prices: we check each view against the agreed products and prices.
outcome: Each brand, market or channel gets its own catalog view with the right products and prices.

steps: Agree the search facets, synonyms, merchandising rules and recommendations for each page type with your merchandisers.
Set them in Commerce Optimizer and check that storefront events arrive.
Train your merchandisers to run them.
asks: Your merchandisers for the setup and training sessions
risk: Recommendations that show nothing: we check storefront events arrive before the recommendations go live.
outcome: Your merchandisers run search, recommendations and merchandising rules themselves in Commerce Optimizer.

steps: Agree with your report owners which measures their reports need.
Set the tables and columns to sync in the Data Warehouse Manager.
Build the calculated columns for the agreed measures and check them against Commerce.
asks: Your report owners for the measure sessions
risk: Numbers that do not match the store: we check each calculated column against Commerce before reports use it.
outcome: Your data warehouse holds the tables and measures your reports need, checked against the store.

steps: Agree the dashboards your teams need, such as sales, customers, products and acquisition sources.
Build the dashboards and reports in Commerce Intelligence.
Check each number against Commerce and walk your teams through reading and filtering them.
asks: Your report owners and the people who will use the dashboards
risk: Dashboards nobody trusts: we check each number against Commerce before the walkthrough.
outcome: Your teams see the store's performance and sales activity at a glance.

steps: Agree who gets which dashboard by email, and how often.
Set up the scheduled emails from Commerce Intelligence.
Show your teams how to export chart data to a CSV or Excel file.
asks: The list of people for each scheduled email
risk: Emails that go to the wrong people: we agree each list before the schedules start.
outcome: Your teams get their reports by email on schedule and export chart data when they need it.

steps: Agree the other data your reports need and where it comes from.
Set up scheduled CSV uploads, or scripts that send data through the Adobe API.
Join the data to the Commerce tables and check the reports that use it.
deliverables: Uploads or API scripts set up
asks: Owners of the other data and its files or API access
risk: Data that stops arriving: we schedule the uploads and check the first runs with the data owners.
outcome: Your reports join store data with the other data your teams track.

steps: Map order, customer, product and stock fields between Adobe Commerce and your ERP, and agree which system owns each.
Deploy the starter kit's actions for each in App Builder and subscribe to the Commerce events, or configure a prebuilt connector from Adobe Exchange where one fits your ERP.
Connect the actions to your ERP's APIs and set retries for failed calls.
Test each data flow end to end with your ERP team.
deliverables: Field map with an owner for each field
asks: API access and credentials for your ERP
Your ERP team for the field map and tests
risk: Orders that never reach the ERP: we set retries and test every flow end to end before launch.
outcome: Orders placed in Commerce reach your ERP without re-entry, and your ERP's stock, prices and order status reach Commerce.

steps: Agree the checkout steps where Commerce needs an answer from your ERP at once, such as taxes or order totals.
Set up the Commerce webhooks that call your ERP and write the answer back into Commerce.
Set timeouts and what happens when the ERP does not answer, and test them under load.
asks: Your ERP team for the endpoints and load tests
risk: A checkout that hangs when the ERP is slow: we set timeouts and a fallback and test them under load.
outcome: Checkout shows your ERP's taxes, totals and payment answers as the shopper buys.

steps: Agree what your team needs to see and do for the back-office sync.
Add the pages to your Commerce Admin with the Admin UI SDK.
Test them with your team: see what was sent, what failed, and send a record again.
asks: The people who will watch the sync
risk: Failed records nobody sees: we show each failure on an Admin page with a way to send it again.
outcome: Your team sets up and watches the back-office sync from the Commerce Admin.

steps: Map your PIM product attributes, categories and media to Commerce.
Build the starter kit's product actions in App Builder that write each create, update and delete to Commerce.
Run the first full load and check it with your product team.
Test that a change in the PIM reaches the storefront.
asks: API access to your PIM
Your product data owner for the attribute map
risk: Product data overwritten in the wrong system: we agree which attributes the PIM owns before the first load.
outcome: Your product team keeps product data in the PIM, and Commerce shows it without a second round of entry.

steps: Agree with your order management team which system owns order status, stock and shipments.
Build the integration on the starter kit in App Builder, or configure a prebuilt connector from Adobe Exchange such as IBM Sterling Order Management.
Send each order and bring back order status and shipments with tracking numbers.
Test returns and cancellations end to end.
asks: API access to your order management system
Your order management team for the tests
risk: Shoppers who see the wrong order status: we test every status change, return and cancellation end to end.
outcome: Your orders reach your order management system as they are placed, and shoppers see the status and tracking it sends back.

steps: Agree when the store asks your order management system for stock, such as add to cart and checkout.
Set up the Commerce webhook that asks for the stock status and writes the answer back.
Set what happens when the system does not answer, and test it under load.
asks: Your order management team for the endpoint and tests
risk: Overselling when stock runs low: we check stock live at the agreed points and test the fallback.
outcome: Shoppers only buy what your order management system says is in stock.

steps: Map your warehouse locations to Commerce inventory sources.
Build the starter kit's stock and shipment actions in App Builder so stock and shipments with tracking numbers reach Commerce.
Send orders to the warehouse system.
Test a full order from purchase to shipment.
asks: API access to your warehouse management system
Your warehouse team for the tests
risk: Stock on the store that does not match the warehouse: we test stock updates for each source before launch.
outcome: The stock your shoppers see follows your warehouse, and shipments reach orders without re-entry.

steps: Take Live Search, Product Recommendations and Catalog Service off your Adobe Commerce.
Install the Commerce Optimizer Connector with Composer and choose the websites, customer groups and store views to sync.
Turn on the integration, run the first sync and check the data in Commerce Optimizer.
asks: Access to your Commerce environments for the install
risk: Search going dark between the old and new setup: we plan the switch and check the sync before the storefront moves.
outcome: Your Adobe Commerce catalog feeds Commerce Optimizer, while Commerce keeps orders and accounts.

steps: Install Adobe's Commerce Optimizer Connector for B2B on your Commerce.
Sync the shared catalogs and check each one shows as a private catalog view.
Test what each company account sees.
asks: A list of your shared catalogs and the companies on each
risk: A buyer who sees another company's catalog: we test what each company account sees.
outcome: Each of your business buyers sees its own catalog through Commerce Optimizer.

steps: Define the product attribute metadata your catalog needs in Commerce Optimizer.
Map your PIM's products, categories and prices to the Data Ingestion API.
Build the job that sends creates, updates and deletes.
Run the first full load and check the Data Sync page.
deliverables: Field map to the Data Ingestion API
asks: API access to your PIM, or exports from it
risk: Products that cannot be found: we define the attribute metadata before any product is sent.
outcome: Your catalog in Commerce Optimizer comes straight from your PIM.

steps: Set up Adobe's Commerce Salesforce Connector in App Builder for your Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C, or a sync job for another platform.
Schedule the syncs and run the first full load.
Check catalog and prices in Commerce Optimizer with your merchandisers.
deliverables: Connector or sync job set up
asks: Access to your commerce platform's catalog and price APIs
risk: Prices that differ between the storefront and checkout: we check prices in Optimizer against your platform.
outcome: Your catalog and prices reach Commerce Optimizer from your commerce platform on schedule.

steps: Agree how shoppers move from the new storefront to your platform's accounts, cart and checkout.
Build the integration with API Mesh, App Builder or your platform's APIs, adapting Adobe's checkout starter kit for Salesforce Commerce Cloud where it applies.
Test sign-in, cart, checkout and a full order with your team.
Hand over how the integration is built and run.
asks: API access to your platform's shopper, cart and checkout services
Your platform team for the tests
risk: Lost carts between the storefront and checkout: we test sign-in, cart and a full order end to end.
outcome: Your shoppers browse on the new storefront and buy through your platform's cart and checkout.

steps: Create your storefront project on Edge Delivery Services with Adobe's Site Creator and point it at your Commerce Optimizer instance.
Build the product detail, search and category pages from Adobe's ready-made storefront parts.
Brand the pages and test them against the agreed designs.
asks: Your approved designs and brand assets
A GitHub repository for the storefront code
risk: A storefront that does not match the brand: we test each page against the agreed designs.
outcome: Your shoppers browse a fast storefront on Edge Delivery Services, fed by Commerce Optimizer.

steps: Agree with your DAM owner how product images carry their SKU and are approved.
Configure AEM Assets for Commerce Optimizer to turn on Product Visuals.
Check that approved images show on the storefront.
asks: Your DAM owner to agree the image rules
risk: Images on the wrong product: we agree how each image carries its SKU before Product Visuals is turned on.
outcome: Your product images are approved in AEM Assets and reach the storefront without re-uploads.

steps: Set up a read-only database user and the SSH tunnel from your Commerce database.
Connect the database to Commerce Intelligence and check the host key.
Choose the first tables to sync and check the first sync.
deliverables: Database connection through an SSH tunnel
asks: Your database administrator for the user and the tunnel
risk: An unsafe database connection: we use an SSH tunnel and a read-only user, the way Adobe recommends.
outcome: Commerce Intelligence reads your Commerce data safely, ready for reports.

steps: Set up a Salesforce user that can read the agreed objects.
Connect Salesforce to Commerce Intelligence and choose the tables to sync.
Join them to the Commerce data for the agreed reports.
asks: Your Salesforce administrator for the read-only user
risk: A report that mixes up customers: we agree how Salesforce and Commerce records match before joining them.
outcome: Your reports put Salesforce leads and opportunities next to Commerce orders.

steps: Connect your Google Ads account to Commerce Intelligence.
Check that campaign tracking on the storefront ties orders to campaigns.
Build the report of campaign cost against the lifetime value of the customers each campaign brought.
asks: Access to your Google Ads account
risk: Orders that cannot be tied to campaigns: we check campaign tracking before the report is built.
outcome: You see which Google Ads campaigns bring customers worth more than they cost.
